page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Managed via a KVM hypervisor, this instance features 24 physical CPU cores supporting simultaneous multithreading for a total of 48 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of memory, providing a strict 2.0 GB RAM allocation per core ratio. The CPU topology features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware acceleration for AVX-512, VAES, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server does not include local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the processing capabilities of the instance in the top 25% across multiple compute-heavy evaluation suites. Multi-core performance is demonstrated by a stress-ng score of 73776.27, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 18295.0, and a software compilation score of 46733.0 using Clang. In database tests, it achieved 64.43 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and a PassMark database operations score of 22342.17. While small-block cached memory bandwidth performs in the top 25% at 3646.1 GB/sec, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds average 113.72 GB/sec and 83.95 GB/sec respectively, reflecting standard memory subsystem throughput under heavy streaming.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio maximizes core density relative to memory, making the server cost-efficient for pure computational processing where high memory overhead is unnecessary. Without bundled local disk space, storage requirements must be fulfilled externally via network storage. The instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, code compilation, image processing, ray tracing, and in-memory key-value caching.

The system includes support for AVX-512 and cryptography instruction sets but omits local storage. Benchmark data places its multi-threaded processing power in the top 25%, with high performance in software compilation, Geekbench multi-core tests, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 64 million operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory bandwidth remains within average ranges. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks by eliminating unnecessary memory overhead. This instance is best suited for CI/CD compilation, multi-threaded batch processing, image rendering, and high-throughput key-value stores.
